rows.description: Decipher old and otherworldly script with scholarly fluency — ritual markings, ward anchors, contract notation. Passive identification on contact with inscribed stone or bound material; reading tells you what it SAYS, not whether it is safe.

rows.name: Silent Image
rows.description: Create a purely visual illusion no larger than a 15ft cube; you can move it. Physical interaction or an Investigation check reveals it is false.

rows.name: Silent Stalker
rows.description: You move without sound. Floorboards, gravel, dry leaves and armour make no noise for you; a creature cannot detect you by hearing alone, and Stealth checks ignore penalties for noisy footing.

rows.name: Siphon Life
rows.description: Drains 3d6 hit points from the target directly into you — what it loses, you gain.

rows.name: Slayer of Legends
rows.description: The creatures out of old stories are just bigger quarry: your weapons wound anything however warded, and no aura of terror, majesty or size makes your hands hesitate.

rows.name: Sleep
rows.description: Roll 5d8: that many hit points of creatures fall unconscious, starting with the creature with the lowest remaining hit points and working up until the pool runs out. Undead and creatures immune to charm are unaffected; damage or a hard shake wakes a sleeper.

targets.from: creatures in a 20ft sphere, weakest first
targets.to: creatures in a 20ft sphere, lowest remaining HP first

rows.reason: The latest owner save defines ascending remaining HP order.

rows.name: Sleep of the Dead
rows.description: Feign death on yourself or a creature you touch — indistinguishable from a true corpse (no breath, no pulse). A self-cast always lasts the full duration.

rows.name: Small Size
rows.description: You are Small: advantage on Stealth to hide behind larger creatures and you can move through a larger creature's space, but you have disadvantage attacking with Heavy weapons.

rows.name: Sneak Attack
rows.description: Double the attack's damage dice when you have advantage, are unseen, or the target is flanked by an ally. Once per turn.

rows.name: Sorcerous Restoration
rows.description: Ten quiet minutes give back what a night gives other casters: recover half your mana. Once per day — a sorcerer who catches their wind is a sorcerer rearmed.

rows.name: Soul Cage
rows.description: Imprisons the target's soul inside a prepared gem; the body collapses comatose. Shattering the gem frees the soul. Fails against creatures more powerful than the caster.

rows.name: Soul Puppet
rows.description: Pour a bound soul into a fresh corpse: the dead creature walks again with its own memories and skills intact — a thinking servant, not a shambler. It knows exactly what it owes you.

rows.name: Soul Steal
rows.description: Your blade drinks the soul of what it cuts: choose one ability the victim possesses and it becomes yours for the next 4 hours, and theirs no longer while you hold it. You may hold three such abilities at once; while all three are held the blade takes nothing new until one expires or you release it. Releasing is a moment's will, and returns the ability to its owner if they live.

rows.name: Soulfire
rows.description: A bound soul is fuel: consume one to regain mana equal to the soul's level, or to cast your next spell as if one tier higher. The soul is spent forever — it does not pass on, it burns.

rows.name: Sovereign of the Night
rows.description: CAPSTONE. From one dusk to the next dawn the night is yours: every shadow a door, every darkness your eyes and ears, every dark thing yours to command. One night to move an army unseen, empty a fortress, or visit every enemy you have at once. Then the sun rises, and the debt is even.

rows.name: Speak with Dead
rows.description: Ask a corpse (with a mouth, dead no more than 10 days, not undead) up to five questions; it answers briefly and cryptically from what it knew in life.

rows.name: Spectral Binding
rows.description: Binds an undead target to a place or object against its will; it cannot stray more than 60ft from its anchor, and its rage tends to show.

targets.to: 1 undead

rows.reason: The description covers undead generally, not only ghosts or spirits.

rows.name: Spellblade
rows.description: Casting and striking are one motion: a spell you cast travels through the steel and lands with the blow, so the cut and the magic arrive together. The spell's own cost is still paid and its save still applies; what you gain is that no enemy gets the moment between the incantation and the stroke.

rows.name: Spider Climb
rows.description: The target climbs sheer walls and ceilings with hands free, moving at its normal pace across any solid surface.

rows.name: Spike Growth
rows.description: The ground in a 20ft radius sprouts spikes (difficult terrain); a creature takes 2d4 piercing for every 5ft it travels through the area.

rows.name: Spirit Guardians
rows.description: Spectral guardians swirl in a 15ft aura; hostile creatures there move at half speed and take 3d8 (WIS save half) when they enter or start their turn there.

rows.name: Spirit Walk
rows.description: Sleep, and send your spirit out in the totem's shape for an hour — scout the pass, circle the camp, whisper to your kin in their dreams. Your body lies defenseless meanwhile.

rows.name: Spiritual Weapon
rows.description: Create a floating spectral weapon; a bonus action moves it 20ft and makes a melee spell attack for 1d8 + your spellcasting modifier force.

rows.name: Split Weave
rows.description: Your mind holds two workings at once: sustain two concentration spells simultaneously. Losing one does not shake the other.

rows.name: Star Fall
rows.description: Stars fall from the heavens pummeling the earth when they land.

rows.name: Stonecunning
rows.description: While underground or touching stone you always know your approximate depth and direction; advantage on checks about the origin or construction of stonework.

rows.name: Storm Shroud
rows.description: Your rage wears weather — choose it: lightning (attackers take 1d8 back), thunder (your blows throw foes off their feet), or frost (everything near you slows). The sky above you agrees with your mood.

rows.name: Strength of Legend
rows.description: Your feats of strength exceed the mortal: hold the falling gate on your shoulders, bend the portcullis, throw a spear the length of a field, drag the beached warship to the water. Bards argue over which of the stories about you are true; all of them are. Feats that would rival giants may demand a check — the GM narrates the rest as fact.

rows.name: Stunning Blow
rows.description: When you hit, you may forgo the damage entirely and strike to stun instead — the pommel to the temple, the flat of the blade behind the ear. The target makes a CON save; on a failure it is stunned for one round and its guard is wide open. Any given creature can be caught by this only ONCE: a foe who has felt it never falls for the same blow twice.

rows.name: Succor
rows.description: Fills the target with an overwhelming sense of calm and security.

rows.name: Suggestion
rows.description: You plant a suggestion no more unreasonable than something the target might plausibly have thought; on a failed WIS save they remember it as their OWN idea and will argue for it to others as such. Ordering them into obvious harm breaks it immediately.

rows.name: Summon Animals
rows.description: Summon fey spirits in beast form (their total power scaling with the slot) that obey your commands and fight for you until the spell ends.

rows.name: Summon Item
rows.description: Summon Item — Teleports a small item to the hand of the rogue. Works on any item within 30 feet if the rogue knows its location. Does NOT require line of sight.  The Rogue must be aware of the item they're summoning, ex: "I summon the ring from the safe" works, but "I summon whatever is in the safe" does not.
rows.reason: The description explicitly specifies thirty feet, not one hundred.

rows.name: Sunbeam
rows.description: A beam of brilliant sunlight blazes from your hand in a 60ft line — 10d8 radiant, CON for half, the failed save also blinding until your next turn. You can sweep it to a new line each round. It is true sunlight, with everything that means for creatures that fear it.

rows.name: Sundering Stroke
rows.description: Your blade cuts magic as though it were rope: sever a standing enchantment, cut a summoned creature from the anchor that holds it here, part a wall of flame or force to walk through. Effects sustained by a living caster within reach may resist with a contest of their will against your strike; unattended magic simply parts.

save.to: living caster within reach may contest will against your strike; unattended magic does not resist

rows.reason: The description explicitly permits a contest for actively sustained magic.

rows.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
rows.description: Disadvantage on attack rolls and on sight-based Perception checks while you, or the thing you are looking at, is in direct sunlight.

rows.name: Superior Darkvision
rows.description: See in darkness within 120ft as though it were dim light, in shades of grey — the extended sight of the deep-dwelling races.

rows.name: Sure Shot
rows.description: Once per combat, declare the impossible shot — a ricochet off a helm, a bank off the temple bell, a needle threaded through an arrow slit at extreme distance. The attack hits and is a critical hit no matter how absurd the path; if any part of the target can be seen, it can be killed. The GM narrates the path the shot takes.

rows.name: Surge
rows.description: Once per rest, take one additional action on your turn — a second attack sequence, a dash, a shove, a shout that rallies the line. The surge is a burst of trained speed, not magic.

rows.name: Swift Quiver
rows.description: Your quiver refills itself faster than you can empty it. While the spell lasts you loose two extra ranged attacks each round, the ammunition dissolving to mist after it lands.

rows.name: Taunt
rows.description: You make yourself the only thing in the fight worth killing — a bellow, an insult, a raised visor. For 3 rounds every foe who heard you attacks YOU if able, leaving your companions unmarked. Ordinary foes simply comply; named or formidable ones may resist with a WIS save.

targets.from: foes who can see and hear you
targets.to: foes who hear you

rows.reason: Hearing is sufficient in the description; sight is not also required.

rows.name: Telekinesis
rows.description: Move a creature or heavy object up to 30ft each round by thought alone — an unwilling creature contests your spellcasting with its STR each round it is held. Fine work at a distance is yours too: thrown levers, turned keys, knots untied.

rows.name: Telepathy
rows.description: You open a private two-way channel of thought with one creature you can see. Words and images pass instantly and silently; the other party knows exactly who is speaking and may simply refuse to answer.

rows.name: Terrifying Frenzy
rows.description: Your frenzy is a weapon everyone else feels: foes who watch you drop one of their own must check their nerve (WIS) or give ground.

rows.name: Terror in the Dark
rows.description: Foes you strike from darkness or ambush must check their nerve (WIS) or panic — a camp you hit at night starts breaking before it forms ranks.

rows.name: Thaumaturgy
rows.description: A minor divine display: boom your voice, flicker flames, cause tremors, sound a phantom noise, or fling open unlocked doors/windows.

rows.name: The Battlefield Is a Board
rows.description: You see the whole engagement at once: where reinforcements will enter, when morale will break, which flank is soft, what each combatant is about to attempt. The GM tells you the true state of any fight you can see, and you are never surprised by a development a soldier could have foreseen.

rows.name: The Beast Beneath
rows.description: Your body answers the wild directly: your unarmed strikes and grapples land like a great beast's (a foe you grapple cannot break free without magic), and on all fours you outrun horses.

rows.name: The Blade Keeps Faith
rows.description: Once, when death takes you, the bond refuses it: you wake whole where your bonded weapon lies, hilt already in your hand, however far that is from where you fell. What happened to you still happened — the wound, the fall, the grief of those who watched — you simply are not dead of it.

rows.name: The Blessing Holds
rows.description: Your boons outlast the danger that prompted them. Any blessing you lay on a companion runs until your next rest instead of fading with the fight — a party that travels with you travels blessed.

rows.name: The Called Shot
rows.description: Your strikes find the places that matter — joints, arteries, the gap in the plate. Wounds you deal are graver than they have any right to be: foes bleed, limp, and favor a side, and they remember who gave them the scar. The GM narrates your solid hits as telling ones.

rows.name: The Casing Eye
rows.description: One look at a place and you know it: where the valuables are, where the strongbox hides, who carries the keys, and every way out — including the ones the owner has forgotten. The GM answers honestly; things concealed by magic may stay hidden.

rows.name: The Challenge
rows.description: Once, call out any creature by name. It must meet you alone in single combat, and the world clears a circle: while the duel holds, no creature, spell, or power outside it may touch what happens within, and neither of you may leave until one yields or falls. The fight itself is still yours to win — the circle only makes it fair.

rows.name: The Dark Between
rows.description: Pull others through with you: carry companions along a Shadow Walk, or drag an enemy into the cold between (CHA resists) and finish the conversation there, in a realm where every advantage is yours. Its native things treat you as one of their lords.

rows.name: The Falling Star
rows.description: Call a piece of the sky down: 4d10 radiant in a 10ft ring and every foe inside knocked from their feet. The crater glows until dawn, and nothing inside its light can hide from you — not behind stone, spell or skin.

rows.name: The Final Accounting
rows.description: CAPSTONE. Declare the Accounting against your named enemy: neither of you can die, flee or be aided until one yields or falls. Every debt settles inside that circle.

rows.name: The First Beast
rows.description: Wear the First Beast — the shape all animals remember in their bones. For a scene, everything wild within a mile answers its cry as kin, and nothing mortal that sees it ever quite settles on what it was.

rows.from: the first blow is the last
rows.key: the first blow is the last
rows.name: The First Blow Is the Last
rows.description: Your first strike against a creature that does not suspect the attack is an automatic critical hit. Against ordinary folk the fight is usually over before it begins; against hardened or named foes it opens with the worst wound they will take.

rows.name: The First Fire
rows.description: CAPSTONE. Set the First Fire in the wound: the dead thing burns for a single heartbeat and stands back up new-grown and whole. The fire keeps your warmth as its tithe — ever after, flames bow away from you, and you will never be warm again.

rows.name: The Gentle Hand
rows.description: Your healing pool doubles, and Lay on Hands now mends minds as well as bodies — madness, despair and magical corruption end at your touch.

rows.name: The God of Battle Attends
rows.description: Call your deity onto the field, and it comes visibly — a wave of standing light, a shadow in armor twelve feet tall — and fights beside you for that encounter, as capable as you are. Everyone present sees it. Word of it travels ahead of you.

rows.name: The Great Spirit's Voice
rows.description: Every beast of your totems' kind within the valley answers your call, and the spirits of the wild deal with you as an equal, not a guest.

rows.name: The Green Ash
rows.description: Ground your fire has touched is yours for a season: it regrows overnight — greener, taller, wilder — and while you stand on land you have burned and reborn, your casts cost one less mana and fire cannot harm you at all.

rows.name: The Green Vow
rows.description: You swore to the life older than the gods: wild places accept you as kin, your smites bloom with thorned light, and once per scene the vines answer you — grasping, tripping, holding fast.

rows.name: The Half-Form
rows.description: Take the middle shape: your hands and voice with the beast's strength and senses — cast, speak, climb and rend in the same body.

rows.name: The Impossible Shot
rows.description: Once per scene, make the shot no one else would attempt — through the arrow slit, the rope at fifty paces, the apple off the moving cart. Declare it; it lands.

rows.name: The Impossible Theft
rows.description: Once, steal a thing no hand should hold: a god's flame, the luck of a house, a word from a language, the color from a king's banner. The theft is real — you hold it and the owner lacks it — and the world adjusts around the fact. It creates a possession, never unwrites the past; how the stolen thing behaves in your keeping is the GM's to narrate.

rows.name: The Inevitable End
rows.description: Once, name a target. From that moment their death is a matter of when, not if: the story bends toward the ending you have chosen — doors sit unlocked, guard shifts change early, the poison is on the right shelf, the storm grounds their ship. The world supplies opportunity, never the kill itself; you must still take it, and the target may yet make their ending costly.

rows.name: The Knee
rows.description: The weight of your god hangs on your voice. Small commands spoken directly — kneel, drop it, wait, speak — land unless the target has real cause to resist, and even then defiance is visible effort. You never puppet a body; you press a will, and its owner is awake for every moment of it.

rows.name: The Last Great Hunt
rows.description: CAPSTONE. Name a single creature the object of your Last Great Hunt: no distance, disguise or plane hides it from your pursuit, and when you finally close, your killing shot cannot be prevented — only survived.

rows.name: The Last Red Day
rows.description: CAPSTONE. Declare the Last Red Day: until the battle ends you cannot die, cannot tire, and cannot be stopped by anything smaller than the battle itself. When it ends you sleep for a week — win or lose.

rows.name: The Law
rows.description: CAPSTONE. Speak one decree over a place and it becomes law in the oldest sense: the land itself enforces it. No blood spilled in this valley. No lie spoken in this city. It holds until a god's own authority overturns it, and your name is on it forever.

rows.name: The Long Hunt
rows.description: Your Hunter's Mark never fades until you release it. You know the direction and freshness of your quarry's trail anywhere in the region, and it cannot lose you by mundane means.

rows.name: The Long Night
rows.description: CAPSTONE. You are the thing veterans warn recruits about. Declare a night yours: until dawn, within a mile, the darkness answers to you — who sleeps, who wakes, who is found, and who never is.

rows.name: The Missive
rows.description: Your compulsion no longer needs your presence. A command under your seal, or carried by a messenger in your name, binds as though you spoke it eye to eye — distance was the defense, and there is no defense.

rows.name: The Moving Heavens
rows.description: The constellations answer mid-fight: wear two at once and swap either each round. The sky over your battles is always the sky YOU need — dark for your rogues, bright for your archers, starless and silent for your escape.

rows.name: The Named Enemy
rows.description: Speak a wrongdoer's name before witnesses: against them you have advantage on everything — striking, tracking, resisting their arts — until justice is done. Choose carefully; the oath remembers.

rows.name: The Oath
rows.description: A promise spoken to you binds. The oath-breaker knows the instant they break it, and so do you, wherever you are — and misfortune of your god's choosing dogs them until amends are made. Only words offered willingly can bind; a forced vow is just noise.

rows.name: The Old Light
rows.description: CAPSTONE. Kindle the Old Light — the sun the first forests grew under: within a mile, corruption burns out of land and folk alike, the wild's dead rise as allies for one battle, and what you plant that day cannot be killed by anything younger than the world.

rows.name: The Old Switcheroo
rows.description: Your invisible Mage Hand exchanges two objects of a size it can carry, and both holders go on believing they hold what they held. A creature actively watching the objects may contest with Perception against your Sleight of Hand.

rows.name: The Plan Holds
rows.description: Once, lay out a plan aloud, step by step. For as long as the party follows it, it works: each step succeeds as described — the guards are where you said, the timing lands, the door is unbarred. The plan runs until the objective is achieved, a step is abandoned, or someone betrays it. The world may complicate the aftermath, never the steps themselves.

rows.name: The Progenitor's Due
rows.description: CAPSTONE. Speak the true name in your blood and your ancestor answers: the progenitor dragon itself comes, in the flesh, disposed to treat you as kin. What it does when it arrives is its own will — dragons are not tame. But it came for you, and the world saw it come.

rows.name: The Read
rows.description: One look at a fighter — a guard's stance, a duelist's first pass — and you know their style, their training, roughly how dangerous they are, and the mistake they are likely to make. The GM answers honestly; creatures beyond mortal warcraft may remain opaque.

rows.name: The Return
rows.description: CAPSTONE. Ask for one person back and be answered. Whatever remains of them — a body, a scrap, a name — they return whole and themselves, however they died and however long ago.

rows.name: The Shadow Half
rows.description: Your shadow can leave you: a second self of dark that walks, watches and whispers back what it sees. While it is out you cast a shadow that is not yours, and the observant notice. If it is destroyed you feel it, and it returns only at nightfall.

rows.name: The Shirt Off Your Back
rows.description: You can steal what is being worn, held, or watched — a sword from a hand, a ring mid-handshake, the medallion from a neck at conversation distance. An aware creature contests with Perception against your Sleight of Hand; when you win, the loss goes unnoticed until it matters.
rows.reason: The description explicitly allows theft at conversation distance rather than requiring touch.

rows.name: The Sky Entire
rows.description: Bring the sky down to arm's reach for a scene: your party walks on air that holds, falls simply refuse to happen, every foe stands lit by prosecutor starlight (no hiding, no feints, no borrowed faces), and one star keeps an old promise — the first ally who would die that scene, instead, does not.

rows.name: The Standing Ward
rows.description: You ward a place by walking its bounds with the blade drawn. While you keep the ward, no magic enters it unbidden — spells cast from outside fail at the line, and things that travel by magic arrive somewhere else — and you know the moment any arcane trespass is attempted, and from where. The ward ends when you leave the place or set it down.

rows.name: The Story Runs Ahead
rows.description: You set a rumour loose about yourself or another; by the time it reaches its destination it has become true in the small ways a story needs to be — the debt was paid, the guard was bribed, the heir was seen in the city. It creates circumstance, never undoes what has already happened, and never directly harms a creature.

rows.name: The Turning Tide
rows.description: Once per combat, call the moment that turns the fight: trip the champion, disarm the captain, feint the line open, rally the wavering. Against ordinary foes the maneuver succeeds exactly as narrated; named or formidable foes contest it with their own warcraft.

rows.name: The Unbroken Line
rows.description: While you stand, allies within your aura cannot be moved, felled or made to flee against their will. Lines break where you aren't.

rows.name: The Unseen Path
rows.description: Once per round, step from one shadow into another you can see. The dark is a hallway only you have the key to.

rows.name: The Walking Tempest
rows.description: Stop pretending to be a person: become the storm outright for a scene — a moving column of wind, frost and lightning that armies cannot hold and arrows cannot find. Chain Lightning and Thunderwave cast themselves each round, and every blow carries Booming Blade at triple strength.

dice.from: Chain Lightning + Thunder Wave each round; blows carry Booming Blade at triple strength
dice.to: Chain Lightning + Thunderwave each round; blows carry Booming Blade at triple strength

rows.name: The Word
rows.description: Speak one short command in your god's own voice, and every creature that hears it obeys for one action. Nothing immediately self-destructive can be commanded, and named foes get a WIS save; the rest simply do it, and remember afterwards that they did.

rows.name: The Yoke
rows.description: Bind a defeated or helpless creature into your service: awake, aware, resentful and obedient. You give orders and it carries them out hating every step — you see nothing through its eyes and speak nothing through its mouth; it serves, it is not worn. Release it, or die, and it is free.

rows.name: Threat Taxonomy
rows.description: On first contact with an unknown individual, compile a rapid threat-and-asset assessment — physical tells, visible capabilities, social patterns — and update it continuously thereafter. Observation and inference, not mind reading.

rows.name: Three Sisters
rows.description: Raises up to three corpses as ghouls that obey your spoken commands; at greater power the dead rise as wights or worse.  Up to three undead may be controlled simultaneously through this spell.

rows.name: Thunderwave
rows.description: A wave of force: 2d8 thunder (CON save half); creatures that fail are also pushed 10ft away. Audible out to 300ft.

rows.name: Tide of Shapes
rows.description: Shift without count or cost, flowing form to form mid-motion — bird to bear mid-pounce. Your enemies fight a different animal every round and never the one they planned for.

rows.name: Tides of Chaos
rows.description: Chaos likes you. When you gamble — a reckless casting, a mad plan, a coin-flip moment — fortune leans your way (advantage). In exchange your magic sometimes answers with an idea of its own: a surge the GM narrates, wondrous or inconvenient, never nothing.

rows.name: Tip the Scales
rows.description: Your first strike each round against a wounded or oversized foe deals +2d6 — the larger the target, the surer your point finds the seam.

rows.name: Totem Aspect
rows.description: The spirit stays after the rage: Bear hauls like an ox team, Eagle reads a hillside a mile off, Wolf tracks by scent alone at a dead run.

rows.name: Totem Spirit
rows.description: A spirit walks in your skin — choose it: Bear (halve all damage while raging), Eagle (no one you charge escapes, no one you flee catches), or Wolf (every ally fighting beside you strikes harder). The totem can be renegotiated only at a sacred site.

rows.name: Trackless Step
rows.description: Leave no trail in natural terrain; cannot be tracked by nonmagical means while moving through wilderness at a careful pace.

rows.name: Trance
rows.description: Meditate 4 hours (semi-aware) to gain the full benefit of an 8-hour long rest; you do not sleep.

rows.name: Travelling Wounds
rows.description: Transfers wounds from one target onto another: heal the first by up to 4d8, and an unwilling second target takes exactly what was healed (CON negates).

rows.name: Turnabout
rows.description: Once, at a moment of your choosing: you and another creature exchange places entirely — position, bonds and restraints, conditions, and the blame the situation carries. The tyrant stands in the cell wearing your charges; you stand where they stood. From that moment everyone present proceeds as though it had always been so, and acts on it.

rows.name: Two Hearts, One Life
rows.description: Death cannot part you: when either of you falls, the other may share its own life to pull them back (split your remaining HP between you). And once — only once — one of you may take the other's death entirely, whatever its cause.

rows.name: Two Totems
rows.description: A second spirit accepts you: carry both totems' gifts at once. Shamans argue about whether that's allowed. The spirits don't.

rows.name: Undead Sense
rows.description: You sense the presence of undead and fiends within 30ft before you see them — roughly where and that they are there, not precisely what.

rows.name: Undead Thrall
rows.description: Your Raise Thrall servant persists permanently until destroyed, gains bonus HP equal to your INT modifier, and can follow simple multi-step orders — go to X and perform task Y.

rows.name: Undying Green
rows.description: The first time each day you would fall, you don't: life floods back at half strength, and green shoots rise in your footprints. The old life does not let go of its sworn.

rows.name: Undying Rage
rows.description: Frenzy no longer ends while enemies stand and costs no exhaustion after — and the first time each day you'd drop mid-frenzy, you stand back up at 1 HP with a 100% damage bonus until the fight ends.

rows.name: Unmoored Sense
rows.description: As a bonus action, attune briefly to the nearest disrupted or unanchored obligation within 60ft. You do not learn its contents — only its weight (trivial, significant, or catastrophic) and roughly how long it has been loose.

rows.name: Unraveling
rows.description: Decay reaches the immaterial: end one active spell or enchantment you can see, or silence a magic item until dawn — its virtue rusts like everything else.

rows.name: Unraveling Presence
rows.description: Probability frays around you. Locks slip, arrows curve, the one loose stone finds an enemy's foot; within 30ft the improbable becomes merely uncommon, and it is never on the other side. A GM who plans around you plans in ranges.

rows.name: Unsettling Presence
rows.description: Your uncanny aspect unnerves others: advantage on Intimidation checks.

rows.name: Vampiric Assault
rows.description: Blood and vitality stream out of every creature in the cone — 12d6 necrotic (CON for half), and you heal half of the total drained.

rows.name: Vampiric Charm
rows.description: The promise of death's defeat is intoxicating: the target saves or becomes your thrall — willing, adoring, obedient. A new saving throw may be rolled every dawn.

rows.name: Vampiric Courtesan
rows.description: Summons a spectral courtesan who embraces your foes — 2d6 necrotic per strike, healing you for the same amount.

rows.name: Vampiric Touch
rows.description: A melee spell attack; 3d6 necrotic and you regain HP equal to half the damage dealt. You can attack again each turn while you concentrate.

rows.name: Venomous Undergrowth
rows.description: Poison vines grow from the floor ensnaring opponents in the target area.  Saving throw vs. poison or suffer poison  damage.
rows.reason: The described save concerns poison damage, not the separate poisoned condition.

rows.name: Ventriloquism
rows.description: Your voice issues from somewhere else — a doorway, a rafter, a statue, another person's mouth. Anything you could say, you can say from there. A suspicious listener may make an INT check to place the trick.

rows.name: Visitation
rows.description: Step through death's door and out again: vanish and reappear beside any corpse you can sense within range. The fresher the corpse, the surer the arrival.

rows.name: Voice of the Land
rows.description: The land within a mile confides in you: ask it what walks, what sickens, what hides. Its answer is always true and always partial — the land has its own sense of humor.

rows.name: Volley
rows.description: With one action, make a ranged attack against up to 2 targets within your weapon's range.

rows.name: Wall of Blades
rows.description: A whirling wall of razor-edged spectral blades. Creatures passing through it, or starting their turn inside it, make a DEX save against 6d10 slashing; the wall grants three-quarters cover to those behind it.

rows.name: Wall of Fire
rows.description: A sheet of roaring flame springs up on a line or ring you choose; creatures in its space when it appears save DEX against 5d8 fire. One side you pick is the hot side: creatures ending their turn within 10ft of it, or passing through the wall, take 5d8 fire outright.

rows.name: Wall of Force
rows.description: An invisible, utterly impassable barrier. It takes no damage from anything, blocks all physical and magical passage, and cannot be dispelled by ordinary means — only disintegration or planar travel gets past it.

rows.name: Wall of Misdirection
rows.description: A wall that shows each viewer something plausible and wrong — open road where there is a cliff, blank stone where there is a door. Creatures may pass through it freely; one who studies it and succeeds on an INT check sees it for what it is, and can then tell others.

rows.name: Wall of Stone
rows.description: Solid, nonmagical stone rises from the earth in shapes you choose — a wall, a bridge, a ramp, an enclosure (DEX to slip out before it closes). Held for the full duration, it becomes permanent, ordinary stone.

rows.name: War Priest
rows.description: Prayer and blow are one motion. You never have to choose between casting and fighting on a turn, and armor, shield and weapon never hinder your magic — a spell of yours has been swung as often as spoken.

rows.name: War Shape
rows.description: Your Wild Shape is built for the front line: combat forms beyond your years, shifting instant, and the beast's hide takes the first wounds meant for you.

rows.name: Ward Architecture
rows.description: Trained in the structural logic of protective wards: identify trigger conditions, recognition mechanisms, and whether a ward targets by intent versus by bloodline or status. Cannot always disable what it identifies — but always knows enough to warn.

rows.name: Ward of Protection
rows.description: Spend 10 minutes inscribing a temporary ward on a surface or object. For 24 hours, a creature attempting to alter, forge, or destroy it must succeed on a WIS save or be compelled to stop and reconsider. It delays and deters — it does not prevent a determined actor permanently.

rows.name: Wave of Scarabs
rows.description: A swarm of spectral scarabs erupts in a 30ft cone; each creature takes 3d6 necrotic (DEX save half).

rows.name: Weapon Bond
rows.description: You bond one weapon to yourself in an hour's ritual. It returns to your hand when called — thrown, dropped, disarmed, confiscated, buried, or an ocean away — and it cannot be taken from you while you live. You may hold one bond at a time; bonding another releases the first.

rows.name: Weapon Mastery
rows.description: No penalty for using improvised or unfamiliar weapons — proficient with anything wieldable.

rows.name: Wear the Sky
rows.description: Star-charts live under your skin: each night choose a constellation to wear — the Archer (bolts of starlight, 1d8 radiant, 60ft, no mana), the Chalice (your healing spells splash 1d6 to a second ally within reach), or the Serpent (you shed dim starlight, and foes who strike you from beside it take 1d6 radiant back). The chosen stars glimmer through your skin while you work.

rows.name: Weight of Account
rows.description: As an action, speak a target's outstanding obligations aloud — real or symbolic. It makes a WIS save or is stunned for one round as the full weight of its debts, kept promises, and broken ones settles on it simultaneously.

rows.name: Where The Light Dies
rows.description: Night itself takes your side: once per day, drown a battlefield in a darkness only you and your allies see through, for a whole scene.

rows.name: Whirl of Bones
rows.description: Shattered bone orbits you in a grinding storm — 3d8 slashing each round to everything within 10ft, and arrows must find you through the whirl.

rows.name: Wild Shape
rows.description: Transform into a beast you have seen, up to a CR limit that scales with level. You take on its stats; you revert at 0 HP or when you choose. Gear melds. Cannot cast spells while shaped until high level.

rows.name: Wind Walk
rows.description: You and your companions become wisps of cloud — flying at tremendous speed (300ft), resistant to weapons, unable to act on the world. Reverting takes a full minute of stillness, and the whole party reverts together or not at all.

rows.name: Wings
rows.description: They were always there, waiting. Wings tear free when called and fold away to nothing — true flight, your own, in any armor, at any hour.

rows.name: Wither
rows.description: Kills plant life outright — crops blacken, vines slacken, a tree dies from the roots up. Plant creatures instead take 4d8 necrotic, CON for half.

rows.name: Witnessed Once, Worked Once
rows.description: Once per day, work a spell you do not know but have seen worked in your sight — friend's blessing or enemy's curse — once, exactly as it was done, at its normal cost.

rows.name: Word of the Score
rows.description: Rumor of treasure finds you: word of every notable score — vaults, hoards, relics, shipments, hidden things — reaches your ears through fences, beggars, and thieves' talk. When you arrive somewhere new, the GM tells you what the local underworld knows is worth stealing, and roughly what stands in the way.

rows.name: Wordless Command
rows.description: Your allies fight as though the battle were rehearsed: a glance repositions a companion, a nod springs the ambush, a raised fist holds the line. Whenever having a plan would matter, the party is treated as having one — even when there was no time to make it.

rows.name: Wrath That Walks
rows.description: Your reputation does half the work now: the corrupt across a region know you are coming, and their servants must check their nerve or abandon them first.

rows.name: Wyrmform
rows.description: Take the full shape of the dragon whose blood you carry — wings, breath, bulk and the fear that comes with it — for a scene. What you do wearing it is remembered.

rows.name: Zone of Truth
rows.description: Sanctify a 15ft-radius zone: each creature makes a CHA save on entering or starting its turn there; on a failure it cannot speak a deliberate lie while inside. You know whether each creature passed or failed. The compelled can still be evasive, answer selectively, or stay silent.
